text.content:
-   Order of the Argent Wolf

    -   Based out of Castlemarch

    -   Rivan Greymane runs the AW Den in Kergrin, out of his store
        called Greymane’s Curiosities

        -   Rivan will relay info that Lady Amara was the one who killed
            Aerithon’s master, Gideon Rowan
        -   Rivan is unsure as to who or how he was betrayed
        -   To complete his training / initiation Aerithon will need to
            visit the order’s HQ in Castlemarch, upon which he would
            earn his silver fang / weapon.
        -   Rivan will write two letters of introduction – one to get
            the party into Castlemarch and another to get Aerithon to
            the head of the order, Old Grey One, Arnmar Carhice.

You go back to Greymane’s curiosities to inquire about the spell book.
Rivan has a line on a crafter that can make one. It will be 50 GP in
expenses and 130 GP for the item, for 180 GP total. It would also take
one week to make.

You recognize the symbols of the order of the Argent Wolf in his shop
and on his person, and reveal that you are a member. You and he discuss
your situation and the fate of your master Gideon Rowan. Rivan shares
with you that Lady Amara was the one that killed him and destroyed his
house. Rivan is not sure who or how he was betrayed.

You and Rivan discuss your training. He tells you that you will need to
go to Castlemarch and see the head of the order, the Old Grey One,
Arnmar Carhice, who will assign your trial to complete your training.
Typically, the trial is in two parts, one performed alone to represent
the lone wolf, and one with a party, to symbolize working as a pack. At
the completion of training, you would be initiated as a full member of
the order and able to progress in levels. You would also receive the
trademark weapon of the order, a longsword known as a ‘Silver Fang.’

Rivan gives you a leather packet of some documents he asks you to
transport to Arnmar. He also gives you two letters of introduction, one
to the Castlemarch guards and one to Arnmar Carhice.

---
